A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MultiADS and contain readable main texts, equations, tables, figures and supplementary material. Content can be reliably matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original MultiADS segmentation and detection results, component ablations and qualitative evaluations in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds MultiADS results under a batched zero-shot setting.

M1.justification: Appendix 11.2.3 adds a batched inference variant using a memory bank of unlabeled test-image patches and quantile-based neighbor scoring. This extends the existing memory-bank approach; the CLIP backbone, adapters, defect-aware prompts and training losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The same five industrial datasets, including real and simulated MAD, remain covered. V2 adds a batched zero-shot scenario on MVTec-AD and VisA, allowing joint access to unlabeled target images.

E2.justification: New Table 22 compares MultiADS with ACR, MuSc and AnomalyDINO at two resolutions, using published baseline scores. V1 explicitly excluded MuSc and AnomalyDINO from comparisons. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds an evaluation protocol constructing reference memory from the entire unlabeled test set. Table 13 also replaces VisA's combined-category accounting with assignments to constituent defect categories. The PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun; their stated training settings and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V1 Figure 12's candle case study, covering missing/extra wax, color spots and melted wax, is removed. Existing component, prompt-transfer and backbone ablations remain. MAD-sim and MPDD seen/unseen-defect analyses move from Table 2 to appendix Table 21 without changed results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new quantile operation is an inference rule, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 22 reports batched image-level AUROC of 96.1% on MVTec and 93.1% on VisA for MultiADS; MuSc is reported at 97.8% and 92.8%, respectively. These are additional-setting results, not improvements over v1 under identical conditions. Retained performance tables are numerically unchanged; the candle qualitative results are removed.

T1.justification: V2 adds mathematical definitions of the batched memory bank, similarity-score set and quantile-based score in Equations (7)-(9), motivated by predominantly nominal patches. This is a limited formal extension without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: zero-shot multi-type anomaly segmentation, defect-aware supervision through KBA, and strong binary zero-/few-shot performance. The added appendix experiment does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets batched inference as domain adaptation and explains why anomalous memory entries motivate quantile-based scoring under a mostly-normal-patch assumption. Existing discussions of missed defects, background false positives and insufficient global context remain.

D1.justification: V2 supplies an explicit MultiADS code link and documents how VisA images labeled combined are reassigned to individual defect categories. V1 only mentions prompts accompanying source code. Most implementation settings remain unchanged, and the new quantile parameter's numerical value is not supplied.

R1.justification: V2 adds the ACR reference, Zero-shot Anomaly Detection via Batch Normalization, and attributes its batched adaptation to AnomalyDINO. Previously excluded batched approaches become explicit comparison points; the broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 makes grammatical edits, shortens the few-shot and AnomalyCLIP descriptions, reorders prompt examples, adds acknowledgements and reorganizes appendix subsections. The main narrative and most prose remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 22, relocates part of Table 2 into appendix Table 21, and enlarges the dense Real-IAD statistics display by splitting it into Tables 17-18. Appendix tables and figures are regrouped, and the candle figure is removed. Most existing displays retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: V2 adds a useful batched comparison, clearer code-access and annotation information, and more readable dataset tables while preserving the original quantitative evidence. Gains are limited: the new quantile parameter remains unspecified, the relationship between relabeling and retained experiments is unclear, and one qualitative case study is removed.
